links.reason: The blessing ends on தீதுதீர் சிறப்பின் தென்னனை and the king says தென்புலங் காவல் என்முதற் பிழைத்தது, so the later scene does reverse the inherited fame. But a wish for a faultless line and a king's confession that it failed first with him are not incompatible claims; this is a fulfilment-by-reversal, better typed develops.

The pairing is real: line 130 (கற்ற கல்வி அன்றால்) refuses learning its own worth and 131-137 put its end in curbing hatred (செற்றம் செறுத்தோர்), ending hunger (அரும் பசி களைந்தோர்) and love for all (அன்பு ஒழியார்), against Kural 2's நற்றாள் தொழாஅர். But the claim the note leans on sits in line 130, outside the unit, and 132 defines 'those who live' (வாழ்வோர் என்போர்), not the learned, so the parallel needs some generosity.
links.text_issue: Unit starts at 131, after the line 130 statement about learning that the link depends on.

links.reason: Neelakesi 533 charges that naming what one holds unreal (பொருளின்மை) again and again cannot establish மெய்யுரை; Kural 292 excuses a falsehood only when it yields புரைதீர்ந்த நன்மை. The couplet is about a benevolent lie, not the semantics of conventional names, so reading it as settling the Buddhist dispute stretches it.

The deity says a violent deed's வல் வினை ஒழியாது and that it comes near (வந்து அணுகும்) and returns in a later birth (மீண்டுவரு பிறப்பின்), having come here (ஈங்கு வந்து) to harm the prince; Naladiyar 101's deed seeks its doer (தற்செய்த கிழவனை நாடி) like the calf. The epic carries the search across a death, which the quatrain does not state; 'does not remember' is an embellishment but not central.

602 puts the fruit in the continuum running on from the doer (அவன்வழித் துன்னுஞ் சந்தானத் தொடர்ச்சி... பின்னை அது பெறும்), while Naladiyar 101 has the deed find the very one who did it (தற்செய்த கிழவனை). On the reading that கிழவன் is a persisting owner the two conflict, and the note correctly gives 602 as the Buddha's (refuted) view.

Kanchanan's rage (இகல் எரி பொத்தி) is real anger, so the theme meets Kural 305. But the couplet says anger kills its owner (தன்னையே கொல்லும்); in the epic it kills another and the angry man lives on, and the killing and the clinging deed lie outside this unit, which ends with him hiding. Reading 'kills oneself' as 'a clinging deed' stretches the couplet.

Both accounts give five categories (நுண்பொருள் ஐந்து / நூற்பொருள்கள் ஐந்து), and only Neelakesi names மற்கலி as god where the Manimekalai has வரம்பு இல் அறிவன். The two are not in conflict, since Makkali can be the boundless knower, so qualifies overstates; and the 'shared spokesman's name' rests on புராணன் vs a பூரணன் drawn from another verse, not on 671.

The vari's கறைகெழுவேல் கண்ணோ கடுங்கூற்றம் and மடம்கெழுமென் சாயல் மகள் take up the couplet's கூற்றமோ கண்ணோ பிணையோ மடவரல், with Death, eye and innocence joined; the stanza makes Death become the girl, a real development of the mixed look into a transformation.

Line 109 கூடலும் ஊடலும் கோவலற்கு அளித்து does name both halves of Kural 1330's ஊடுதல்/கூடி முயங்க cycle. But reading அளித்து as a courtesan's trained art is generous (it can simply mean she granted him love's play), and the 'whose feeling it is' gain is the grader's question, not the couplet's.

673 likens the unseen Lord to வரையா வகை வானிடு வில், and 684 takes the same simile back (வானிடு வில்லின் வரவறியாத வகையன் என்பாய்) to show the rainbow arises when கதிர் வீழ் புயல் மேல் — a claim and its refutation inside the debate, with the note accurate on both.

Kural 1066 says nothing degrades more than asking (இரவின் இளிவந்தது இல்), and lines 71-74 have Manimekalai call பத்தினிப் பெண்டிர் இடூஉம் பிச்சை ஏற்றல் பெருந் தகவு உடைத்து, a defensible conflict. But that line is outside the unit; within it the crowd's grief (சிந்தை நோய் கூர) is that the girl Udayakumaran loved carries a bowl, not the Kural's shame of asking, and an ascetic's alms is a different case from the householder's begging the couplet addresses.
links.text_issue: The claim the tension rests on (71-74) falls just after the unit's end at 70.

links.reason: Neelakesi 18 has renouncers who strive with knowledge that their deeds wear away (ஞானமொடு செய்வினைகள் நைய முயல்வாரும்), and Tirumanthiram 1527 ends the malas when தன்செயல் அற்றால் under grace come as guru. On the self-effort reading this is the effort-versus-grace tension the brief asks for, but 18 is a passing description of the land, not a stated doctrine, so the conflict rests on one verb.
links.text_issue: Line 3 division (கானமொடு கல்லடரு ளில்லிடரு நீங்கி) is uncertain.

links.reason: 670's ஆத்தனு நூலும் பொருளு நிகழ்ச்சியும் match the king's heads in 172 (முதலவன், நூல், முடிபொருள், நுதலிய பொருள்நிகழ்வு, நுங்கோள்), now put by Neelakesi herself to the Ajivika. The later verse answers the earlier by turning the judge's frame into her method, as the note says.

The patikam's உரைசால் பத்தினிக்கு உயர்ந்தோர் ஏத்தல் does begin to be acted out when Kuttuvan takes பொருவறு பத்தினிக் கற்கால் from the Himalaya. But the unit shows the stone taken after battle, not anyone praising her, so it is a thesis-and-plot fulfilment the story already carries; the praise by kings comes later.

Manimekalai resolves வஞ்சியுள் புக்கு மா பத்தினி தனக்கு எஞ்சா நல் அறம் செய்குவல், and at the Vanji shrine the maid asks the pathini மணிமேகலை துறவுங் கேட்டாயோ. The two epics meet at the same shrine from both sides, which is a specific and true cross-epic tie.

The unit sets out a logical rule that absence is shown by non-appearance (தோன்றாமையில், இன்மையின் கண்டிலம் முயற்கோடு); Kural 351 warns that taking பொருளல்லவற்றைப் பொருளென்று causes மாணாப் பிறப்பு. The couplet's மருள் is a spiritual delusion, not an error of inference about pots, so the 'procedure' joins them only by the word 'unreal'.

Maadalan's ஊடற் காலத் தூழ்வினை யுருத்தெழ repeats the patikam's ஊழ்வினை உருத்துவந்து ஊட்டும், and வடதிசை மன்னர் மணிமுடி யேறினள் makes உயர்ந்தோர் ஏத்தல் literal. The note is accurate on both ends and teaches shows where the morals are fulfilled.

Kannaki's dream ends on a good that would be laughed at (யான்உற்ற நல்திறம் கேட்கின் நகைஆகும்), and 23:198-199 fulfils it as she rises in the sky car with Kovalan (கோவலன் றன்னொடு வான வூர்தி ஏறினள்). A dream and its event, with a plausible reason for the laughter.
links.text_issue: Lines 51-54 are dense and the referent of உறுவன் is not certain.

links.reason: The image court weeps when அரைசுகோல் கோடினும், and in Madurai the king is தளர்ந்தசெங் கோலன் and says யானே கள்வன், so the theme of the bent sceptre is shared. But the two cities are not linked by the plot or by any answer, and teaches rests on an unsupported absence ('Madurai has no such image'), which neither text states.

The epic's herds fill the yards of the smith, drummer and bards (கொல்லன் துடியன் ... பாணர்தம் முன்றில் நிறைந்தன), and Purananuru 257's raider who took herds by the score has a pot showing no curd (வெண்கோள் தோன்றாக் குழிசி). Read together the giving away explains the empty pot, a specific gain on both sides.
links.text_issue: The augur and toddy seller named in teaches come from lines 132-135, outside the unit.

links.reason: The eyes throb in counted order on the festival day (எண்ணுமுறை இடத்தினும் வலத்தினும் துடித்தன), Madhavi's the right, and at the end of the Kaanal Vari ஊழ்வினைவந்து உருத்தது as Kovalan loosens his embrace and leaves. An omen and its fulfilment, with karma named at the fulfilment.

The epic does show renunciation and death from the same news (இறந்ததுயர் எய்தி ... மெய் விடவும் / புண்ணிய தானம் புரிந்தறங் கொள்ளவும்), against Naladiyar 53's நிலையாமை கண்டு. But deaths are exactly a sight of impermanence, and Madhavi gives a reasoned motive (மணிமேகலையை ... கணிகையர் கோலங் காணாது ஒழிக), so calling the epic's renunciations unreasoned shock overstates the contrast.

The Manimekalai's Ajivika gives water சீதத்தொடு சுவை and fire தெறுதல், while 688 attacks a version where வண்ணாதி எல்லாம் நிலப்பால், leaving the other elements unseen. The difference between the two reports is real and the note states it accurately.

491 says the five aggregates arise together and perish in one moment (உடனே அவை தோன்றி ஒரு கணத்துள் கெடுமே); 506 gives a causal order, உணர்ச்சியினால் செய்கை ... செய்கையினால் உழப்பு. A claim and the argument that refutes it, as the note says.

The herald bids debaters பட்டி மண்டபத்து ஏறுமின் and part without செற்றமும் கலாமும், and kaathai 27 has Manimekalai hear the schools in turn. But the shared topic is all the pair has: the 'disguise' and the claim that no debate is ever shown in Puhar are not in either unit, and 27 is still a hearing among public schools, not a private search.

வேலை அகழால் அமைந்த அவனி is the stock 'sea-moated earth', and the venba is a wish (வாழியரோ), not a claim the city will last; neither the venba nor its lines name the festival. Turning a conventional epithet and a blessing into a tension with Manimekalai's அணி நகர் தன்னை அலை கடல் கொள்க stretches the words.

Mokkala argues that endless things cannot be known to an end (எல்லையில் பொருள்கள் ... எல்லையின்று அறியின்), and 451 answers that the Lord's knowing is not sequential (முறைபடும் அறிவிலன்) and nothing hides from it. The pair shows the point of disagreement, the assumption of serial knowing.

1075 says fear is the conduct of the base (அச்சமே கீழ்களது ஆசாரம்); 1018 says shamelessness is a fault virtue itself would blush at (அறம் நாணத் தக்கது). These are compatible statements on different subjects, and teaches ('look alike and differ in source') is not stated by either.

Neelakesi asks whether women are goods fit for alms (உறுபொருள் பிச்சைக்கு உரியார்கள்) and whether their takers are not thieves (கள்ளர்கள் அன்மை); Kural 221 defines giving by the receiver (வறியார்க்கு ஒன்று ஈவதே). The added condition (give only what is one's own) is true, but the two answer different questions, and the epic side gains nothing specific from the couplet.

The girl sets his own words (இன்னே வருதும் எனத்தெளித்தோரே) against the spring that came without him, and Kural 1151 retorts நின் வல்வரவு வாழ்வார்க்கு உரை. Same refusal of the quick-return promise, and teaches marks a real difference: a retort before parting against evidence gathered after.

The venba bids hearers turn to நல்லறம் since நண்ணும் இருவினையும்; it is moral counsel, not a doctrine of release. Tirumanthiram 1527 is about release when இருவினை நேரொப்பு and grace comes; the shared word இருவினை and different advice for different ends is not an incompatible claim.

Both speak of grey hair (நரை): Naladiyar 11 has the wise renounce in infancy (குழவியிடத்தே துறந்தார்) foreseeing it, and Purananuru 191 credits a good wife, children, king and சான்றோர் for having none. The contrast of values is real, but they answer different questions (foresight of death versus why he looks young), so the tension depends on the note's hedged reading.

The townspeople ask whether வளையாத செங்கோல் வளைந்தது and தண்குடை வெம்மை விளைத்தது, and the queen's dream opens with குடையொடு கோல்வீழ. The same royal emblems appear as the street's verdict and the palace's omen, a meaningful shared image across scenes.

389 says the lump that perished and the paste that arose are modes while the thing remains (நட்டமுந் தோற்றமு ... உருவிற்கு), and 777 turns the opponent's 'not now, later' into உண்மையும் இன்மையும் for all things. The same Jain doctrine is used against momentariness and against satkarya, as teaches says.

Naladiyar 43 asks whether spices, flowers and பொய்க்கோலம் remove the foulness பெரியோர் saw and gave up; Manimekalai says பூவினும் சாந்தினும் புலால் மறைத்து ... தொல்லோர் வகுத்த வஞ்சம். Same image of adornment hiding the flesh, with the specific turn that the elders see through it in one and devised it in the other.

74 promises பிறவியுட் பிறக்கும் பிணி and the அறவியின் மருந்து; 86 names penance by which the dark karma goes (கருவினை போய் ... தவத்தால்) for the people of கரும நிலம். This is the sermon's own order of exposition, the plot of the teaching rather than an answer or reversal, so the link is thin.

Kural 576 likens those who have eyes but no kindly regard (கண்ணோடு இயைந்து கண்ணோடாதவர்) to மண்ணோடு இயைந்த மரம்; Neelakesi 368 argues trees are living because of swellings and heat. The couplet's tree is a figure for unused eyes, not a claim about whether trees feel, so reading it through the Jain scale of senses rests on the shared word மரம்.

The swing song's ஓரைவர் ஈரைம்பதின்மர் உடன்றெழுந்த போரிற் பெருஞ்சோறு போற்றாது தானளித்த closely follows Purananuru 2's ஐவரோடு ... ஈரைம் பதின்மரும் பொருது ... பெருஞ்சோற்று மிகுபதம் வரையாது கொடுத்தோய். The epic gives the deed to சேரன் பொறையன் மலையன் beside the கடம்பெறிந்த deed, so the shift from a named patron to the line holds.

Valayapathi 4 is spoken to someone (கொள்நீ) by an unknown speaker in a lost scene, and 46 compares a divided woman's mind to oil spread on water. Both are fragments in an editor's order; the 'case for giving them up' that teaches says they complete is a reconstructed argument neither verse states.
links.text_issue: Fragments; order and speakers are editorial.

links.reason: 201 argues that if nothing of the first moment is in the next (முதலது ஒன்று ஆசு அனைத்தும் இல்லையேல்) knowing is impossible, and 518 tests it on a word heard letter by letter (முதலெழுத்துப் பற்றின சித்தம் ... பாழ்படலால்). The general objection is applied to a concrete case.

Madhavi reads a குறிப்பு into Kovalan's songs and sings தானும் ஓர் குறிப்பினள் போல்; at 287-289 Kovalan says she sang ஒன்றின்மேல் மனம் வைத்து, and the narrator adds ஊழ்வினைவந்து உருத்தது. The later passage answers the earlier, and teaches is accurate about the two causes.

Purananuru 65's உழவர் ஓதை மறப்ப, as the Chera sits north, is reversed by the epic's தொடுப்பேர் உழவர் ஓதைப் பாணியும் at Senguttuvan's return. The shared ploughmen's cry as the measure of the king's fortune is real, but these are opposite occasions, not incompatible claims, so tension is the wrong type; and the note's 'shameful death' overstates a king ashamed of a back wound (புறப்புண் நாணி).

claims_rejected.why: the list of topics (தவம், தருமம், சார்பின் தோற்றம்) names teachings without stating them
the hospitable household is described, not stated as a claim
the belief that a spirit guards the grove is reported as hearsay, not a doctrinal claim

claims.gist: a thing is both non-existent and existent, according to where it is
no continuum can cross the gap between a human body and a god's body
good and bad deeds are done through mind, speech and body
an ear that does not hear the glory of Tirumal is no ear
if total destruction is not granted, what stood before remains

claims_rejected.why: the girl as a goddess who brings pain is love-poetry figure

claims.gist: consciousness and pleasure arise from the five elements as intoxication arises from its ingredients
where a life goes after death is set by its deeds and is hard to know
one who loves a life should pity every life
the strong deed of a former killing rose and took the prince's life
if the Buddha had greatness already, his later striving accomplished nothing
qualities and actions are distinct from the substance and come to inhere in it

units.note: Tentative; the verse states the view only to fault it.

claims_rejected.why: the straight sceptre and cool umbrella are description of Madurai, not a claim

claims.gist: for a thing that undergoes no change, the members of an inference all come to nothing
beings born as animals suffer cold, war-wounds, beating for food and nets

units.note: Closer to description than statement; tagged because the sermon states it as the condition of animal birth.

claims.gist: a woman's charms are nothing to an ascetic
the Buddha wanted nothing for himself and suffered for others
the Buddha saves those who come to him

claims_rejected.why: auspicious rites in the street are described, no claim

claims.gist: a valid reason has three marks: present in the subject, present in similar cases, absent from dissimilar ones
sound is impermanent because it is produced, as a pot is
drink leads its drinker to ruin
those who take false conduct for worth do not escape grief
these deeds bring suffering to all who live in the world and must be given up

claims_rejected.why: the hunter who died of grief is an illustration, not a stated claim
narration of the demon's form, no claim
an omen that something will come, not a doctrinal claim

claims.gist: for those born in this royal line, to die of old age is a shame
